title: Redwood discovery - model selection discussion (Nautilus Logistics)
summary: Intro discovery call to scope model selection: customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for multilingual cargo document parsing + agent tool-calling. Key constraints: long-context (16k-64k), multilingual across EN/ES/FR/JP, on-prem requirement for some PII lanes, KMS/HSM for keys. Agreed next step: Redwood to share model perf table, Dedicated pricing tiers, security brief and schedule benchmark run with sample docs.
next_steps: Jordan to send model performance matrix + sample quantization recommendations by 2027-06-11
Sofia to propose benchmark run plan and request sample docs via secure link by 2027-06-14
Customer to confirm scope of PII lanes and list of on-prem regions by 2027-06-16

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-09
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Kim (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood Solutions Eng); Marina Costa (CTO, Nautilus), Devon Park (Head of ML), Ravi Menon (Infra), Aisha Khan (Security), Ben Yu (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick round robin - can each of you say role?
[00:06] Marina: Marina, CTO, we run the logistics platform and we're pushing more ML into docs and agent workflows.
[00:11] Devon: Devon, Head of ML - owning the models and evaluation, we'll be driving the benchmark.
[00:16] Ravi: Ravi, infra, I care about network, VPC, private deploy and egress.
[00:20] Aisha: Aisha, security and compliance, SOC2 and KMS questions.
[00:24] Ben: Ben, product, user cases and throughput targets.
[00:28] Jordan: Great, thanks. Overview: goal today is to understand model selection needs - do you want Hosted, Dedicated, or Private? And what model capabilities are must-haves - long context, multilingual, tool-calling, accuracy for invoices/shipping manifests.
[00:40] Marina: High level - we have two lanes: public-facing features that can use hosted, and internal PII-heavy pipelines that must stay in our VPC or on-prem. So dual mode possibly. Latency sensitive for real-time agent tasks (<=300ms token lat for small replies) and batch parsing where throughput and cost matter.
[01:02] Jordan: Understood. Sofia, can you cover our typical model choices and tradeoffs?
[01:06] Sofia: Yeah, so for open models we typically compare Mistral-family models, Llama-derivatives like LLaMA3 variants, and Falcon. Each has tradeoffs: Mistral tends to be strong on code and instruction-following, Llama3 has big ecosystem and tooling, Falcon is good on shorter contexts and lower cost on some libs. Context length - we see 16k, 32k, up to 64k variants depending on model and quantization. For Dedicated/Private we can support custom kernel paths and larger context with optimized KV cache handling, but it costs more.
[01:38] Devon: For us, long context is big - shipment docs can be 10-20k tokens if you include multiple attachments. We also need good multilingual support - EN/ES/FR/JP - especially Japanese for manifests. Any model that bleeds performance on JP is a no-go.
[01:55] Sofia: Right, so we'd probably recommend a 32k or 64k context model for your pipeline. On hosted we have 32k for certain variants; Dedicated/Private can do 64k depending on GPU and memory - we have customers running 64k on A100-class with custom kernels.
[02:12] Ravi: Quick infra question - if we go Dedicated, is it full isolation? We want no egress for PII lanes.
[02:17] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved capacity with data isolation; for strict no-egress you'd look at Private (VPC or on-prem). We can do Private with our control plane in a customer VPC or full on-prem bundle. There are tradeoffs on management.
[02:28] Aisha: On KMS - do you integrate with customer HSMs? We need key custody.
[02:32] Sofia: Yes, we support KMS integrations and can FIPS/HSM in Private deployments. In Hosted we use our managed KMS by default but do have bring-your-own-key options for Enterprise customers under contract. Sometimes the transcription has typos - e.g., "K-M-S" gets spelled out.
[02:46] Ben: Tool-calling - we need model able to call our microservices for lookups and return structured JSON. Does Redwood support function or tool-calling patterns?
[02:54] Liam: Yep - we support structured function/tool calling and streaming. Important note: some open models need light adapters for deterministic tool-call behavior; we provide tooling in the runtime to surface function schemas and enforce output formats. There can be slight accuracy drift depending on quantization.
[03:10] Devon: About quantization - if we quantize to int8 or GGML-like formats does tool-calling or accuracy degrade?
[03:15] Sofia: There's often a small hit in few-shot reasoning with aggressive quantization - but for many structured extraction tasks it's acceptable. We recommend running your evals - we can run the benchmark on your sample docs.
[03:24] Marina: What's the typical latency difference between Hosted and Dedicated for chat/agent tasks?
[03:29] Jordan: Hosted is optimized for multi-tenant low-latency but Dedicated gives predictable tail latency because you control reserved GPU pools and batching policies. In our experience median is similar, but p95/p99 is better on Dedicated.
[03:41] Ravi: Network egress and peering - we have restrictions that disallow unapproved internet egress from our subnet. How does Private work?
[03:49] Sofia: Private can be deployed inside your VPC with no public internet egress. If you take the on-prem option, the control plane can be air-gapped and logs forwarded to your SIEM. For Hosted, we do have VPC peering options but it still uses our control plane endpoints.
[04:04] Aisha: Audit logs - retention and access control?
[04:07] Liam: We provide per-request audit logs, token-level cost breakdown, and RBAC. For Private, you can choose retention policies and push logs to your S3 or GCS bucket.
[04:15] Jordan: Back to models - Devon, do you have a preferred eval metric? For invoice parsing we usually measure F1 on entity extraction and end-to-end slot accuracy for agent tasks.
[04:24] Devon: F1 for entities, and a custom pass/fail for tool-calls - must return valid JSON schema 98% of the time for critical flows. Also multilingual BLEU-ish metrics for JP/ES.
[04:35] Ben: Also cost target - we need to keep per-document cost under $0.12 on average for batch parsing.
[04:40] Sofia: Noted - Dedicated and Private with batching and KV caching will help. We have Optimize suggestions like smart prefix caching that dramatically reduces token cost for repeated headers and templates.
[04:51] Jordan: Let's walk through a scenario: real-time agent that calls our pricing API - needs latency, secure keys, and tool-calling accuracy. Which deployment?
[05:10] Marina: For real-time public-facing agent we could use Hosted if we can guarantee SLAs and KMS. For PII lanes, Private. So hybrid.
[05:17] Sofia: Hybrid is common; we recommend staging the pilot on Dedicated to validate p95/p99, then expand to Private for PII lanes.
[05:25] Devon: For model selection, is there a single model family that tends to be best for multilingual + long context?
[05:30] Sofia: It's nuanced - Mistral-l3 variants are strong, LLaMA3 has large context variants and good multilingual, and some Falcon forks are optimized for certain langs. We'll send a comparison matrix with accuracy and latency numbers on typical shipping doc tasks.
[05:47] Ravi: Any special infra considerations for 64k context? Memory and kernel changes?
[05:52] Liam: Yes, 64k consumes large KV cache memory and depending on GPU you might need model sharding or sequence-k caching. Our Dedicated config can use multi-GPU sharding and optimized kernels to keep latency sensible. There's sometimes a mismatch in docs - like "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cash" - apologies.
[06:08] Aisha: Compliance - SOC2 and pen tests?
[06:11] Jordan: We are SOC2 Type II and have penetration test reports we can share under NDA. For Private installs, additional compliance can be arranged.
[06:19] Ben: Who will run the benchmark? Redwood or us?
[06:22] Sofia: We can run it - we'll need a sample of 1k documents across languages and labels for evaluation. We'll run on Hosted and Dedicated variants and share delta. Ideally also run on your infra if going Private.
[06:35] Marina: Timeline - we want pilot in Q3 and production for PII lanes by Q4.
[06:39] Jordan: Sounds feasible. Next steps recap: I'll send pricing/model perf, Sofia will schedule the benchmark, and we'll coordinate on sample docs and network details.
[06:48] Customer questions / random clarifications and closing minutes:
[06:52] Devon: Small nit - streaming tokens for partial results? Important for UI.
[06:55] Liam: Yes streaming with incremental JSON patches is supported; some models stream better than others.
[07:01] Aisha: Please include data residency options in the brief.
[07:03] Jordan: Will do.
[07:06] Marina: OK thanks - we'll review the materials.
[07:09] Jordan: Great, thanks all.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-attributed speaker labels and minor transcription errors (proper nouns like "Mistral" sometimes as "Mistrel", "KV cache" as "K-V cash").

End of call.
